The evidence base is the FY2025 print (2026-03-03) and the Q1-2026 call (2026-05-07); no multi-quarter primary transcript exists for this foreign listing, so this case is grounded in those two touchpoints plus the metrics. forcing_function: For deep_value the Forcing Function is: 'What event forces the market to re-rate?' This is the WEAKEST leg of the case and the reason for verdict B over A under the current regime. interrogator_dossier:
# Forensic Dossier — Ariston Holding N.V. (ARIS.MI, Borsa Italiana / Euronext Milan)

**Analyst:** Interrogator (Claude Opus 4.8) · **Signal:** deep_value · **Sector:** Consumer Cyclical (Capital Goods — thermal comfort / HVAC-adjacent)

**Transcript-depth disclosure (read this first).** Ariston is a foreign (Milan-listed) name with **no bundled FMP transcript** and only a thin, syndicated English-language record. I could not access a clean multi-quarter run of primary transcripts. What I *could* verify and read: (1) the **Q1 2026 earnings call** held 2026-05-07 (syndicated transcript via Investing.com — the call on which the stock had already been punished), (2) the **FY2025 results + slides** released 2026-03-03 (the print that sent shares down ~13% on the day), and (3) corroborating analyst/IR data (Simply Wall St consensus, Borsa Italiana ownership filings, the Carrier–Riello and Lennox JV releases, March-2026 buyback filings). I therefore have **two consecutive management touchpoints (FY25 + Q1-26), not the full 8-quarter arc** the template assumes. I will be explicit where a claim is inferred from two data points rather than tracked across many. I have **not fabricated** any quote or figure; everything quoted is from the two events above. Treat the "narrative arc" section as a 2-period read, not an 8-quarter forensic.

---

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

Across the two touchpoints I can read (FY2025 in March, Q1-2026 in May), the core story is **consistent and unusually un-promotional**: *"the European heating market bottomed in 2024, heat-pump electrification is structurally recovering, and we are compounding margin while the top line is flat."* This is a **recovery-and-self-help** narrative, not a growth-stock narrative.

What management **emphasized at FY25 (March 2026):** the margin story above all — adjusted EBIT €193m at a **7.1% margin, +100bps YoY**, framed as proof that the cost base is now leaner than the depressed 2024 trough implied. The second pillar was the **heat-pump inflection**: German incentive approvals of **288,000 units in FY25, +91% YoY**, accelerating into Q4 (31k vs 24k in Q3) and January-2026 (21,300, ~+50% YoY) — explicitly framed as a recovery "despite an overall market contraction to a 15-year low." The third, newer pillar was **two transformational deals**: the **Riello acquisition from Carrier ($430m, closing H1-2026)** and a **Lennox US water-heater JV** targeting a **"$10 billion U.S. wholesale water-heater market."**

What carried into **Q1-2026 (May):** the same margin-discipline framing — Q1 adjusted EBIT **€34m at 5.2%**, "substantially stable year-on-year" — plus a deliberate **damping of near-term expectations**: revenue "substantially flat," profitability "highly seasonal" (~two-thirds in H2), and a pointed reminder that **2026 cash generation is "concentrated in the fourth quarter."** The growth pillars were **pushed further out**: Lennox now explicitly "**significant sales are expected from 2027 onwards**," with 2026 reframed as "setting up organization, product training, and services."

**Thesis shift / contraction:** the **timeline lengthened** between March and May. Heat-pump recovery stayed intact, but the *monetization* of the two strategic deals was visibly deferred (Lennox → 2027; Riello synergies undiscussed). Nothing was dropped, but the **"when does this show up in the P&L" answer moved right.** A growth driver that quietly *appeared* and is now a swing factor: **net debt rising** (€542m → €631m in one quarter) as the Riello cash outlay and seasonal working-capital build hit simultaneously. This is the single most important narrative *addition* — the balance sheet went from a tailwind to a watch-item within one quarter.

---

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)

The screener's multi-year trajectory and TTM block let me test management's three big claims hard. The headline tension: **management's margin story is largely TRUE, but the screener's EPS optics are a statistical artifact that overstates the turnaround.**

| Management claim (FY25 / Q1-26) | What the financials actually show | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| "Adjusted EBIT +100bps to 7.1%; margin discipline working" | Gross margin **45.9% and expanding**; net margin **4.9%**; FCF margin **5.8%**; FY25 adj. EBIT €193m vs ~€160m implied prior. Trajectory: NI **2024 €2m → 2025 €132m**. | **TRUE but flattered.** The margin expansion is real (gross 45.9%, expanding corroborates it). But the *level* (7.1% adj. EBIT) is recovery-off-a-trough, not best-in-class — the screener flags margin **−0.35σ below historical peak**, i.e. still below where this business has run before. |
| "+5488% EPS YoY" (screener) / "strong recovery" | 2024 EPS was **€0.0068** (near-zero) → 2025 EPS **€0.38**. The 5488% is **division-by-a-trough noise**, not underlying growth. 5-yr EPS CAGR is **−4.7%**; revenue 3-yr CAGR only **+3.8%**. | **MISLEADING optic.** Anchor on the trajectory, not the YoY %. EPS in 2021 was €0.46, 2023 €0.51 — 2025's €0.38 is still **below 2021–23 levels.** This is a company that *recovered to sub-peak*, not one that broke out. |
| "Heat-pump electrification is a structural tailwind; +91% incentive approvals" | Revenue growth only **+1.0% YoY / +3.0% organic FY25**; Q1-26 organic "substantially flat." Heat-pump *units* up 91% off a collapsed 2024 base; the broader market is at a **"15-year low."** | **PARTIALLY TRUE / over-weighted.** The unit recovery is genuine, but it is **not yet moving the consolidated top line** — gas-boiler decline (Italy "under pressure," France funding-uncertain) is offsetting it. The mix shift is real; the *net* growth is not. |
| "Two transformational deals (Riello, Lennox)" | Riello $430m closing H1-26; net debt already **€631m, ~2x leverage**. Lennox revenue "from 2027." TTM FCF **€406m** (screener) vs FY25 reported **€125m** — note the screener's TTM FCF looks high vs the company's own €125m FY25 FCF figure. | **CREDIBLE but balance-sheet-financed and back-end-loaded.** The deals are real and strategically coherent, but they consume the balance sheet *now* and pay *later (2027+)*. This is the crux of the valley-of-death. |
| "Confident on full-year guidance (+1–4% organic, 7–8% adj. EBIT)" | Guidance implies a **steep H2 ramp** (Q2 €766m → Q4 €920m vs Q1 €656m). FCF "concentrated in Q4." Beat rate only **1 of 2 quarters (50%).** | **CONDITIONAL.** The full-year math *requires* the back half to deliver. With a 50% recent beat rate and the top line flat in Q1, this is a show-me. |

**Net forensic read:** the *quality* signals corroborate management (Piotroski **8/9**, gross margin expanding, ROE 10.2%, ROIC 6.1%). The *growth* narrative is **richer than the trajectory justifies** — the screener's +5488% EPS and "104% margin of safety" are both partly artifacts of a 2024 trough and a low multiple, not evidence of a breakout. The honest framing: **a structurally sound, family-run cash compounder that fell to ~6.7× P/FCF and 8.5× P/E because the European heating market is at a 15-year low and the recovery is real but slow.**

---

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY

**Rating: STABLE (cautiously confident, deliberately under-promising).** Only two touchpoints, so this is a short read, but the tone is notably consistent and *defensive-leaning*, which for a deep-value name is a feature, not a bug.

- **FY25 (March 2026):** Offensive on margin and heat pumps — "robust operational performance that contrasted sharply with investor sentiment." Management leaned into the self-help story even as the stock fell 13%. Confidence here was **structural** (deals announced, margin target raised to 7–8%).
- **Q1-26 (May 2026):** Tone shifted **from offensive to managing-expectations.** Repeated hedges: "highly seasonal," "concentrated in the fourth quarter," costs "manageable and in line with the guidance," Middle East effects "well under control thanks to the measures." The forward-looking optimism was real but **qualified** — "positive start to quarter two," "remain confident on the guidance." This is the language of a team that knows the market doesn't believe the back-half ramp and is trying to buy credibility by under-claiming Q1.

There is **no detectable shift to euphoria or to crisis** — the band is narrow. The one tonal tell: the deliberate **deferral language on Lennox** ("significant sales from 2027 onwards") reads as management pre-empting an analyst push on near-term contribution. That is honest, but it also concedes that the two headline catalysts **do nothing for 2026 numbers.**

---

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY

**Reliability: MEDIUM.** I lack the multi-quarter guide-vs-deliver history to score this High, and the screener's **50% beat rate (1 of 2 quarters)** caps my confidence. Two specific observations:

1. **FY2025 guidance was met or modestly beaten:** the company delivered the margin expansion it had pointed to (7.1% adj. EBIT, +100bps), and the heat-pump recovery materialized as flagged. That is one clean "delivered."
2. **FY2026 guidance is self-consistent but back-end-loaded and unproven:** +1–4% organic and 7–8% adj. EBIT margin, *confirmed* at Q1 despite a flat Q1 and a near-double-digit decline in the Americas. Confirming guidance after a soft quarter is either confidence or stubbornness; the honest read is that **the full-year number now leans entirely on H2**, and we have no Q2 print yet to validate the ramp.

**Sandbagging pattern:** mild and in the *right* direction for a value name — management is framing Q1 conservatively ("substantially flat," "seasonal") and parking the upside (Lennox, Riello synergies) in 2027. There is no evidence of the opposite (over-promising into a miss). The risk is not credibility-of-intent; it is **credibility-of-the-macro** — the European heating market and Middle East logistics are exogenous and could overwhelm a well-run plan.

---

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS

From the Q1-26 call, the recurring **deflections** were specific and revealing:

- **Lennox contribution:** management explicitly punted — "wait for them to give you the numbers" — declining to quantify the JV's 2026/2027 revenue. Analysts clearly want a number; management won't give one. **This is the single most-pressed, least-answered topic.**
- **Riello performance / synergy detail:** management said they "lack visibility as competitors" pre-close — a reasonable but unsatisfying non-answer on the $430m deal's accretion.
- **Heat-pump vs gas category splits:** management "declined detailed heat-pump vs gas comparisons" and "resisted sharing competitive detail" on granular regional breakdowns. Given that the *entire bull case is the gas→electric mix shift*, the refusal to quantify the crossover is the most important analytical gap.
- **Americas weakness:** management attributed the "negative, close to double-digit" US decline to a tough comp (Q1-25 "exceptionally high" on tariffs/incentives) — plausible, but this is the kind of "one-off comp" explanation that analysts later turn into bad news if Q2 also disappoints.

**What analysts worry about that management isn't fully addressing:** (a) the **back-half ramp credibility** after a flat Q1; (b) **net-debt trajectory** through the Riello close; (c) whether the **gas-boiler structural decline** outruns the heat-pump recovery on a *revenue* (not unit) basis. Management's answers on all three are directionally reassuring but quantitatively thin.

---

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS

🟢 **Gross margin 45.9% and expanding** — corroborates the margin-discipline claim independently of management's framing.
🟢 **Piotroski 8/9, Altman-Z 2.5** — high fundamental quality and adequate (not pristine) solvency for a leveraged industrial.
🟢 **Insider alignment is real:** Executive Chairman Paolo Merloni accumulated **~€2.0m of stock over 12 months**; the company ran a **March-2026 buyback** (treasury to 3.5%, mandated to Mediobanca). Family controls via Merloni Holding S.P.A. — skin in the game and a buyer at these levels. *(Note: the screener's "insider buy ratio 0.00" appears to be a data gap for this foreign listing; the filings show active insider buying — trust the filings.)*
🟢 **Heat-pump leading indicator genuinely accelerating** (Jan-26 approvals +50% YoY) — the recovery is not just a narrative.
🟢 **Margin guidance raised** to 7–8% for 2026 — management putting a number on the self-help.

🔴 **Net debt jumped €542m → €631m in one quarter** (Q1-26), leverage to ~2x, with the Riello cash outlay still to fully land — the balance sheet is the pressure point.
🔴 **Revenue is structurally flat** (+1% YoY, +3% organic, Q1 "substantially flat") — the unit recovery is **not converting to top-line growth** because gas-boiler decline offsets it.
🔴 **Guidance is dangerously back-end-loaded** — Q4 revenue (€920m) must be ~40% above Q1 (€656m); FCF "concentrated in Q4." Any H2 macro slip breaks the full-year.
🔴 **EPS still below 2021–2023 levels** (€0.38 vs €0.46–0.51) — this is a *recovery to sub-peak*, and the screener's +5488% YoY is a trough artifact, not growth.
🔴 **Exogenous fragility:** Middle East/Hormuz logistics, CBAM steel-cost inflation, and French heat-pump subsidy uncertainty are all outside management's control and all hit H2.
🔴 **Dividend track record "unstable"** (historical cuts >20%); current €0.10 (2.7% yield, 28–33% payout) is modest and not a reason to own.

---

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS

- **The "from 2027 onwards" phrasing on Lennox** is the most important subtle tell: management is *protecting 2026* by explicitly disclaiming near-term JV contribution. They are managing the gap between a strategic story (US $10bn TAM) and a numbers story (nothing this year).
- **"Concentrated in the fourth quarter"** appears for *both* revenue ramp and FCF — management is pre-loading the excuse-management for a soft H1 and asking investors to underwrite a Q4 they can't yet see.
- **Shift in how they discuss the US:** at FY25 the US was the *Lennox growth optionality* story; by Q1-26 the US is the *near-double-digit-decline, blame-the-comp* story.
